key_insight: The paper gives an explicit quantum circuit for spatial search on d-dimensional lattices by implementing the discrete-time flip-flop quantum walk with coin-controlled position updates and a simple direction-reversal gate.
engineering_relevance: It turns an abstract quantum-walk algorithm into a hardware-oriented circuit recipe with logarithmic register scaling, making lattice-based quantum search more practical to synthesize and test on near-term devices.
method: Encode opposite directions so they differ in one coin qubit.
Use coin-controlled modular increment/decrement on position registers for the shift.
Apply a single X gate to reverse the direction label after each move.
evidence_signal: The circuits were verified against theoretical dynamics on 2D and 3D periodic lattices, extended successfully to a 2D non-periodic boundary case, and the depth/resource trends were evaluated with noise robustness under a CX depolarizing model.
watch_item: The depth and noise performance may still be constrained by CX-heavy synthesis, and scaling beyond the tested lattice sizes or to more irregular boundary conditions may increase overhead.
paper_title: Quantum Circuits for Quantum Spatial Search on $d$-Dimensional Lattices
